Description Of Work

The Director of Broadcast Engineering & Technology provides strategic and operational leadership for the Nebraska Public Media’s broadcast, production, and distribution technologies across statewide television and FM radio platforms. The position serves as a bridge between traditional broadcast engineering and modern IT-centric workflows, bringing a forward-looking perspective on emerging technologies, risks, and opportunities.

Nebraska Public Media offers a full spectrum of communications services to the citizens of Nebraska, the nation and the world. Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively with technical staff, executive leadership, and external stakeholders.

Seven (7) years’ experience in broadcast engineering or technology origination within the media or comparable industry.

Job Description

The Sr. Director, Technical Program Management will lead a global technical program management organization responsible for driving execution of strategic AI/Datacenter Infrastructure Power package engineering and new product introduction (NPI) programs. This leader will partner closely with Package Engineering Directors, Power product group partners—especially Design, Application, and Marketing teams—Product, Reliability, Quality, Operations, Supply Chain, and key OSAT/CM partners to ensure programs meet committed schedules, quality and reliability objectives, and production readiness requirements. The role will establish strong program governance, identify and escalate critical risks early, and lead cross-functional technical task forces to resolve development challenges that threaten quality, reliability, yield, manufacturability, or schedule.

The organization will also provide technical program management leadership at key OSATs, ensuring consistent execution, issue escalation, and alignment between Renesas development teams and external assembly partners.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Lead the global Technical Program Management (TPM) organization supporting AI/Datacenter Infrastructure Power NPI and package engineering programs.

Partner with Package Engineering Directors who lead technical package development programs, providing program-level execution leadership, governance, and accountability.

Establish and drive end-to-end NPI program plans, milestones, critical paths, resource alignment, risk management, and executive reporting to ensure committed schedules are achieved.

Create a disciplined program management operating model covering development, qualification, customer requirements, production readiness, ramp, and transition to volume manufacturing.

Proactively identify technical, quality, reliability, supply, manufacturing, and schedule risks; establish mitigation plans and escalate critical issues with clear recommendations and decision points.

Lead cross-functional technical task forces for major development challenges, particularly issues affecting quality, reliability, yield, manufacturability, qualification, or NPI schedule.

Drive structured problem solving and closure of critical issues using data-driven methods, root-cause analysis, risk assessment, and clearly defined corrective/preventive actions.

Coordinate closely with Package Engineering, Power product group partners—especially Design, Application, and Marketing teams—Product Engineering, Reliability, Quality, Operations, Supply Chain, and other functional leaders to remove execution barriers and maintain program momentum.

Establish program dashboards and management systems that provide transparent visibility to milestones, critical path activities, risks, issues, action owners, and recovery plans.

Lead technical program management activities with key OSAT/CM partners, including program reviews, milestone tracking, issue escalation, recovery plans, qualification readiness, and production ramp execution.

Ensure execution of Engineering Build Requests (EBRs) per committed schedule at each OSAT, regularly tracking overall EBR progress, identifying delays, and driving timely recovery actions.

Develop and lead TPM teams located at strategic OSATs, ensuring alignment with Renesas priorities, technical teams, and global NPI schedules.

Ensure OSAT/CM development activities, DOE, process optimization, qualification, process-window verification, production controls, and ramp readiness are aligned with overall NPI program objectives.

Drive timely resolution of process integration and assembly issues that could impact product quality, reliability, qualification, yield, or customer commitments.

Ensure effective transition from development and qualification into production, including readiness reviews, ramp monitoring, issue management, and sustained execution.

Establish standardized program management processes, templates, metrics, escalation mechanisms, and lessons-learned practices across the global organization.

Provide concise, fact-based executive communication on program health, critical risks, schedule recovery, resource needs, and decisions required from senior leadership.

Build strong relationships with OSAT/CM executive and technical leadership to improve responsiveness, accountability, and execution of critical AI/Datacenter Power programs.

Develop the technical and leadership capabilities of the TPM organization and establish a high-performance, execution-focused culture.

Support package technology roadmap execution by translating strategic technology priorities into executable development programs, milestones, resources, and deliverables.

Address internal and external customer-impacting issues in partnership with Marketing, Product, Quality, Operations, and Package Engineering organizations.

LEADERSHIP & ORGANIZATIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES

Lead and develop a global team of Technical Program Managers supporting strategic AI/Datacenter Infrastructure Power programs.

Set organizational priorities, staffing strategy, performance expectations, and development plans aligned with business growth.

Establish clear accountability between Technical Program Managers and Package Engineering technical leaders while avoiding duplication of technical ownership.

Create a culture of urgency, fact-based decision making, cross-functional collaboration, ownership, and rapid issue resolution.

Drive consistent execution standards across internal teams and strategic OSAT locations.

Qualifications

QUALIFICATIONS

Doctorate, Master’s, or Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, Chemistry, or a related technical discipline.

15–20+ years of relevant experience in semiconductor engineering, product development, applications, package development, NPI, manufacturing, technical program management, or a closely related field.

Demonstrated experience leading complex semiconductor NPI programs involving package development, assembly, qualification, reliability, and manufacturing ramp.

Strong understanding of semiconductor product development process, package and assembly processes.

Experience in Power Management products, particularly power SiP/modules, Smart Power Stages, Vertical Power Stages, Power Modules, Discrete FET packages, battery management system, PMICs, wafer-level and/or flip-chip technologies.

Experience working with OSATs/CMs and managing complex development and production activities across geographically distributed organizations.

Proven track record leading cross-functional technical task forces and resolving complex issues involving quality, reliability, yield, manufacturability, and schedule.

Strong understanding of qualification, reliability, SPC/statistical methods, process development, risk management, and structured problem-solving methodologies.

Exceptional program management skills, including critical-path management, risk management, executive escalation, schedule recovery, and cross-functional resource alignment.

Strong interpersonal, communication, negotiation, and executive presentation skills.

Ability to influence senior technical and business leaders without direct authority and drive accountability across organizational boundaries.

Experience building and leading global teams, including teams in product groups, embedded at external manufacturing or OSAT locations.

Strong analytical skills and ability to translate complex technical issues into clear business impact, decisions, and actions.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

Experience supporting high-growth customer programs.

Experience with Smart Power Stage, Vertical Power Stage, power module, discrete FET, SiC/GaN, DBC/AMB, multi-chip, wafer-level, or advanced interconnect technologies.

Experience with formal technical program management methodologies and portfolio-level governance.

Experience driving customer-critical NPI programs in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

SUCCESS MEASURES

On-time achievement of NPI milestones and customer commitments.

Reduction in schedule delays caused by unresolved technical, quality, reliability, or manufacturing issues.

Timely closure of critical cross-functional task-force actions.

Improved qualification, yield, reliability, and production-readiness performance.

Effective execution and alignment of strategic OSAT/CM partners.

Development of a high-performing global TPM organization and standardized program-management operating model.

This collaborative spirit and mindset drive our semiconductor technology to transform industries and impact millions of lives.

We believe in rewarding our employees with a competitive benefits package alongside their salary. More information will be provided during the hiring process.

In 1968, the New York Stock Exchange began closing on Wednesdays so brokerage firms could catch up on paperwork. Every transaction depended on physical stock certificates being delivered, recorded, and reconciled. Trading had outgrown the infrastructure behind it. The expression “Paperwork crisis” had entered the nation's agenda resulting in other temporary measures like shortened trading days and extending settlement. The industry responded with electronic clearing systems and the establishment of the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC) laying the foundation for markets that could operate at an entirely different scale.

Every share needs an identity, every movement needs a record, and every balance needs to agree with the institutions holding the assets. The best financial infrastructure makes this complexity feel ordinary. Building it takes extraordinary care.

At Mercury, our Investments team helps founders put their capital to work through products like Treasury and Invest. Our Custody team builds the systems underneath that experience: the ledger, security master service, reconciliation, and operational tools that keep customer assets accurately accounted for and give our products a dependable foundation to grow.

We’re looking for a senior engineering manager to lead the Custody team through its next stages of growth and scale to better serve our small and large customers.

As part of this role, you will:

Lead, hire, and develop a team of senior engineers, providing thoughtful feedback and building a trusting and supportive environment.
Own the team’s technical strategy and roadmap, translating Mercury’s investment ambitions into focused priorities and predictable delivery.
Guide the design and evolution of core custody systems, including cash and securities ledgers, security master service, position tracking, and reconciliation.
Partner with product, investment operations, and compliance to turn business and regulatory requirements into well-designed systems, operational controls, and auditable workflows that balance correctness, scale, and maintainability.
Collaborate with Product and Partnerships to align integrations, responsibilities, and technical roadmaps.
Set a high bar for correctness, reliability, and incident response, balancing new capabilities with the maintenance and improvement of critical systems.

The ideal candidate for the role:

Has 3+ years of experience managing highly technical teams.
Has direct experience building or operating RIA and broker-dealer custody systems at scale, including ledgers, security master service, cash and securities reconciliation, and money movement.
Understands the broker-dealer operating model and how responsibilities and data flow across introducing brokers, clearing firms, and custodians.
Has worked closely with compliance and operations teams, translating requirements into practical engineering decisions and effective controls.
Understands the lifecycle of securities and the implications of settlement and corporate actions for customer cash and positions across equities, fixed income, ETFs, and mutual funds.

added.title: Founding Head of Product & Engineering
added.description:
SYNDRI | New York City preferred | Full-time

About SYNDRI

SYNDRI is the world’s first consumer-facing AI jewelry designer. Customers can design custom fine jewelry through conversation, starting with an idea, image, reference or existing piece. They can explore and refine the design visually, send it to pricing, approve the final design and CAD and 3D imaging and have the piece produced by skilled jewelers.

SYNDRI is currently in private beta. The core product is built and we are now focused on refining the experience, expanding the product roadmap and preparing to scale.

We’re looking for our first senior product hire to own that next phase.

The Role

As Founding Head of Product & Engineering, you will work directly with the founder and take ownership of both the product experience and the technical evolution of SYNDRI.

There is a significant roadmap ahead. Your job is to make the product dramatically better: refine the existing experience, decide what should be built next, improve the underlying AI systems and execute quickly.

This is not a traditional Head of Product role where you primarily manage a roadmap and hand requirements to engineers. You should be technical enough to work directly in the product yourself — understanding the codebase, prototyping and implementing improvements, evaluating models and APIs, debugging issues and making informed technical decisions.

You will have engineering support, but you will be the internal technical owner of the product. You should be comfortable getting hands-on yourself whenever that is the fastest or best way to solve a problem.

At the same time, this is not a pure engineering role. You will think deeply about the customer, product experience, roadmap and business - and make decisions about what is worth building in the first place.

SYNDRI sits at the intersection of AI, consumer product, design, ecommerce and physical production. The software needs to feel creative and intuitive while ultimately producing a real object that can be priced, manufactured and delivered. A major part of the opportunity is figuring out how more of that journey can become intelligent, automated and scalable over time.

What You'll Own

Product strategy, roadmap and prioritization

In 1968, the New York Stock Exchange began closing on Wednesdays so brokerage firms could catch up on paperwork. Every transaction depended on physical stock certificates being delivered, recorded, and reconciled. Trading had outgrown the infrastructure behind it. The industry responded with electronic clearing systems and the establishment of the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC) laying the foundation for markets that could operate at an entirely different scale.

SCOPE OF MANGEMENT & SUPERVISION

Manages activities of two or more disciplines within a department. Oversee experienced level professionals and/or may be responsible for subordinate supervisors. Strategic Leadership & Organizational Development

Build a culture of excellence, ownership, and continuous improvement that attracts and retains top documentation talent.
Lead, mentor, and develop a team of engineers and technical staff, providing regular feedback, career guidance, and professional development opportunities

Ability to think and draw conclusions quickly, adapt to change, be open to new ideas, take on new responsibilities, handle pressure, and adjust plans and priorities to meet changing needs

Drive cross-site configuration management maturity — establishing consistent CMP frameworks, CCB governance models, and CM audit cadences.
Serve as the organization's senior escalation point for the most complex documentation, change control, and configuration disputes requiring executive engagement.
Lead the documentation function through major organizational events — ERP migrations, PLM platform transitions, new site launches, or large program onboards.

Represent the documentation function at the executive and customer level, participating in program reviews, contract negotiations, and strategic planning sessions.

Translate customer and market requirements into functional capability investments and process improvements.
Collaborate with product/program managers and cross-functional teams to identify customer needs, allocate resources, and deliver projects on schedule and budget

Ensure compliance with industry standards, local regulations, and safety requirements.

Lead enterprise-level PLM and ERP transformation initiatives, from strategy definition through implementation governance and adoption measurement.
Champion digital transformation of documentation workflows including paperless manufacturing, and AI-assisted document processing.
Establish enterprise KPIs, benchmarks, and maturity models for the documentation function; report on progress to the executive team.
Build technical depth across the sustainment engineering staff through targeted training, knowledge sharing, and hands-on mentoring in in various engineering disciplines.
Ability to conceptualize initial component and system designs with schematics and block diagrams; lead project team execution of assembly, test, debug, and optimization; and organizing results for design reviews and customer presentations.
Provide technical leadership and hands-on contributions across the sustainment engineering lifecycle, including concept development, design, test, and integration activities
Experience designing and developing engineering solutions to overcome component obsolescence
Ensures validation of engineering drawings, specifications, contract deliverables, various software documentation, contract modifications, and design release documents to confirm compliance with customer contract requirements.

Requirements

MINIMUM EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE

120.15 (U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident, or protected individual) due to access to ITAR-controlled technical data.

Who We Are

Oasis Health Partners (Oasis) is building healthier communities by advancing primary care.

We partner with patients, providers, and plans to provide personalized, local care for seniors. We believe that patient needs come first, and that primary care is the foundation of patient-centric healthcare. With Oasis, patients receive better access and care. Providers receive the data, resources, and expertise to be successful in value-based care arrangements. Payors get the benefit of a solution that improves performance, drives growth, and reduces the total cost of care in hard-to-engage markets.

added.description:
In 1968, the New York Stock Exchange began closing on Wednesdays so brokerage firms could catch up on paperwork. Every transaction depended on physical stock certificates being delivered, recorded, and reconciled. Trading had outgrown the infrastructure behind it. The expression “Paperwork crisis” had entered the nation's agenda resulting in other temporary measures like shortened trading days and extending settlement. The industry responded with electronic clearing systems and the establishment of the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC) laying the foundation for markets that could operate at an entirely different scale.

Every share needs an identity, every movement needs a record, and every balance needs to agree with the institutions holding the assets. The best financial infrastructure makes this complexity feel ordinary. Building it takes extraordinary care.

At Mercury, our Investments team helps founders put their capital to work through products like Treasury and Invest. Our Custody team builds the systems underneath that experience: the ledger, security master service, reconciliation, and operational tools that keep customer assets accurately accounted for and give our products a dependable foundation to grow.

We’re looking for a senior engineering manager to lead the Custody team through its next stages of growth and scale to better serve our small and large customers.

Lead, hire, and develop a team of senior engineers, providing thoughtful feedback and building a trusting and supportive environment.
Own the team’s technical strategy and roadmap, translating Mercury’s investment ambitions into focused priorities and predictable delivery.
Guide the design and evolution of core custody systems, including cash and securities ledgers, security master service, position tracking, and reconciliation.
Partner with product, investment operations, and compliance to turn business and regulatory requirements into well-designed systems, operational controls, and auditable workflows that balance correctness, scale, and maintainability.
Collaborate with Product and Partnerships to align integrations, responsibilities, and technical roadmaps.
Set a high bar for correctness, reliability, and incident response, balancing new capabilities with the maintenance and improvement of critical systems.

The ideal candidate for the role:

Has 3+ years of experience managing highly technical teams.
Has direct experience building or operating RIA and broker-dealer custody systems at scale, including ledgers, security master service, cash and securities reconciliation, and money movement.
Understands the broker-dealer operating model and how responsibilities and data flow across introducing brokers, clearing firms, and custodians.
Has worked closely with compliance and operations teams, translating requirements into practical engineering decisions and effective controls.
Understands the lifecycle of securities and the implications of settlement and corporate actions for customer cash and positions across equities, fixed income, ETFs, and mutual funds.

Who We Are

IREX is a global solutions provider that partners with communities and institutions in the United States and around the world to cultivate leaders, expand access to education, and create economic opportunity. With deep expertise, a forward-looking vision, and world-class practices in AI for Education, Future-Ready Workforce, Higher Education Solutions, Leadership Development, and Online Safety, IREX delivers innovative and proven solutions that help people, institutions, and communities thrive in a rapidly changing world.

About The Role

The Director of Information Technology serves as IREX’s senior operational and technical leader for Information Technology and as the designated deputy to the Chief Technology Officer for delegated operational and technical matters. The Director provides technical leadership across cloud and infrastructure, cybersecurity operations, enterprise applications and integrations, AI and automation, service delivery, and technology partners. The Director serves as IREX’s senior technical escalation point and is expected to work directly within technology platforms when needed. As deputy to the CTO, the Director provides operational and technical continuity, independently resolves matters within delegated authority, and represents the technology function as delegated by the CTO.

We’re looking for our next team member – could it be you?

Range: $160,000 - $190,000

What You’ll Do

Technology Operations and Infrastructure

Lead day-to-day technology operations and maintain a stable, secure, scalable, and cost-effective technology environment.
Provide hands-on technical leadership for Microsoft 365, Azure, Entra ID, Intune, Microsoft Defender, networking, cloud infrastructure, endpoint management, and identity and access management.
Serve as the senior technical escalation point for complex issues and participate directly in troubleshooting and resolution.
Establish and maintain architecture, configuration, lifecycle, and operational standards in coordination with the CTO.
Ensure technology platforms are appropriately monitored, maintained, patched, backed up, documented, and supported.
Provide technical direction for IREX offices and programs operating across different countries and technology environments.
Maintain and test appropriate business continuity, disaster recovery, system resilience, and technology recovery capabilities.

Enterprise Applications and Integration

Lead the operational management and technical integration of IREX’s enterprise application portfolio, including ERP, HRIS, CRM, Microsoft 365, collaboration and knowledge platforms, and other business systems.
Work with business owners to translate requirements into practical technical solutions, system improvements, and integration opportunities.
Lead or participate directly in system implementation, configuration, integration, enhancement, migration, and troubleshooting.
Use APIs, scripting, Power Platform, and other integration technologies to improve interoperability and reduce manual processes.
Ensure enterprise applications have appropriate ownership, security, documentation, lifecycle management, integration, and support models.

AI, Automation and Agent Platforms

Partner with the CTO to translate AI and automation priorities into practical technical solutions.
Provide technical leadership for Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Studio, Power Platform, and related AI and automation capabilities.

Cybersecurity Operations and Technology Risk

Implement, operate, and maintain technical security controls across identity and access management, endpoint security, vulnerability remediation, logging and monitoring, and configuration management.
Provide technical oversight of cybersecurity vendors and managed security services, including validating that delivered work meets IREX requirements.
Support incident response, audits, risk assessments, and remediation activities, including evidence collection and technical investigation.
Escalate significant cybersecurity incidents, unresolved technical risks, and proposed exceptions to security requirements to the CTO.

Strategy Implementation & Governance

Implement the IT strategy and governance framework established by the CTO, translating strategic direction into executable workplans, operational practices, and measurable milestones.
Lead execution of delegated strategic initiatives across infrastructure, cybersecurity, enterprise applications, automation, and service delivery to ensure progress against organizational priorities.
Track implementation progress, identify risks or barriers to delivery, and recommend adjustments to timelines, sequencing, or resourcing for CTO review and decision-making.
Establish practical governance routines, documentation, and decision-support processes that improve consistency, accountability, and operational follow-through across IT initiatives.
Ensure technology changes are adopted effectively by the organization through careful planning, stakeholder coordination, communications, training, and post-implementation support.
Provide the CTO with timely updates, analysis, and escalation of issues requiring strategic direction, policy decisions, or executive-level intervention.

Teamwork/Cross-Functional Leadership

Serve as a trusted technology advisor to departments and program teams, helping translate operational needs into practical, secure, and sustainable technology solutions.
Partner with functional leaders to understand business priorities, assess technology implications, and align IT support with organizational goals and user needs.
Influence and guide non-technical stakeholders by clearly explaining technology options, trade-offs, risks, and implementation impacts in accessible terms, building understanding and support for technology decisions and organizational change.
Facilitate cross-functional planning and coordination for technology initiatives that require shared ownership, process changes, user adoption, or operational readiness.
Build collaborative relationships across the organization to improve technology engagement, strengthen adoption of enterprise systems, and support consistent use of tools and platforms.
Represent IT in delegated cross-functional meetings and working groups, ensuring decisions are informed by technical feasibility, security considerations, user experience, and long-term sustainability.

Budget & Vendor Management

Manage technology vendor relationships within delegated areas of responsibility, including coordinating services, monitoring performance, resolving issues, and validating deliverables.
Review and approve vendor invoices within delegated authority, ensuring charges are accurate, aligned with contracted services, and supported by appropriate documentation.
Partner with the CTO and Procurement to support vendor sourcing, renewals, contract coordination, and evaluation of vendor performance and value.
Monitor budget spend for assigned technology services, licenses, tools, and vendor engagements, identifying variances, risks, or opportunities for cost control.
Provide input and analysis to support technology budget planning and forecasting, while recognizing that overall IT budget ownership and final budget accountability remain with the CTO.
Maintain practical oversight of software licensing, subscriptions, support agreements, and managed service arrangements to promote cost-effectiveness, compliance, and continuity of service.

User Support and Service Delivery

Sustain a customer service mindset across IT support and service delivery, ensuring staff receive responsive, respectful, and solutions-oriented support.
Establish and monitor service levels and appropriate performance indicators.
Monitor responsiveness using defined service expectations, such as timely acknowledgment, prioritization, escalation, and resolution of support requests based on urgency, impact, and agreed service levels.
Ensure effective escalation and resolution of complex or high-impact issues.
Identify recurring issues and address underlying technical or process causes.
Promote a culture of accountability and continuous improvement by using service trends, user feedback, and recurring issues to improve processes, communication, and the overall technology experience.
Use ticket trends, service metrics, user feedback, and recurring issue analysis to identify continuous improvement priorities and implement practical changes that improve reliability, user satisfaction, response quality, and service consistency.
Maintain appropriate technical documentation, procedures, knowledge resources, and user guidance.
Build trust with internal users by setting clear expectations, communicating proactively, following through on commitments, and ensuring technology support is aligned with staff needs and organizational priorities.

Our Culture is Our People

At IREX, our culture is built on our people—and on how we work together to create meaningful impact every day. We look for colleagues who bring purpose, curiosity, collaboration, and a bias for action to help strengthen communities and advance our mission.

Successful candidates build trust across differences, move ideas into action, seek new perspectives, adapt to change, and represent IREX with authenticity and professionalism. We value people who bring strong expertise and a generous team spirit to work that advances our mission.

Strong hands-on technical capability, judgment, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to independently troubleshoot complex technology issues and make sound technical and architectural decisions.
Strong understanding of cloud infrastructure, identity, endpoint management, enterprise applications, integration, automation, AI platforms, and cybersecurity.
Ability to move effectively between technical execution and technology leadership.
Ability to independently evaluate and challenge vendor recommendations.
Strong leadership and communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical matters to non-technical stakeholders.

Requirements
